text:
Leah: New dev reported onboarding sample prints INFO lines with no request-id for first few seconds, then later DEBUG lines include request-id. Very confusing during first-run.
Omar: Node or Python sample? Could also be Go/Rust.
Leah: Node to start. Sequence: require('redwood-sdk'), configure logger, init OTLP exporter async, then start server. LOG_LEVEL=info.
Tessa: Sounds like an init-order race where request-id middleware or logger bootstrap happens after some components already logged. If exporter registration mutates logger state, you can see apparent level flips.
Omar: Quick mitigation to ship: 1) call a synchronous initLogger at top of entry (before any imports that may log); 2) add a tiny request-id fallback middleware to set an id immediately for first logs; 3) bump sample dependency to SDK that has the exporter registration guard.
Leah: Any code snippets I can drop in sample quickly?
Omar: Top-of-process pattern (Node):
const { initLogger } = require('redwood-sdk');
initLogger({ level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info' });
// then require app modules that might register OTEL/exporter
// and add this tiny middleware before handlers:
app.use((req,res,next)=>{ req.rid = req.headers['x-request-id'] || `${Date.now().toString(36)}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,6)}`; next(); });
Tessa: For Python: call init_logger(...) at top of wsgi entry file before importing Flask/FastAPI app. For Go/Rust: initialize the SDK logger synchronously before spinning exporter goroutines. Keep parity across languages.
Leah: Another problem: when DEBUG logs do appear they sometimes include emails from headers. Sample currently uses an ad-hoc regex that misses plus signs and subdomains.
Omar: Use the SDK's redact_headers helper if available, otherwise use a robust pattern: (?:[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+)@(?:[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+)\.[A-Za-z]{2,} and add test cases for alice+ci@example.co.uk and bob.smith-qa@sub.domain.io.
Tessa: Also add a tiny integration smoke test in CI: start sample with LOG_LEVEL=info, hit /health once, capture stdout for 2s, assert no DEBUG-level log exists before any line that contains "request-id=". Keep it short and deterministic.
Leah: Any SDK version we should require?
Omar: We added a guard in 1.3.x/1.4.x depending on language that prevents async exporter registration from flipping effective log level. Recommend bumping to >=1.4.1 if available for the sample.
Tessa: One more parity gotcha: Python logging config can be lazy if you use dictConfig after importing libraries that log during import. Ensure init_logger runs before importing instrumented modules. Mirror same note in quickstart docs.
Leah: Good call. I'll open a small PR: add early init snippet to top of entry, insert req-id fallback middleware, replace regex with SDK redactor calls, add the tiny CI smoke test, and upgrade the SDK dep.
infra-bot: Created issue devex/samples#6230: "onboard: early logger init + request-id fallback + header redaction parity + startup smoke test + SDK bump"
Omar: Ping me on the PR; I'll review the Node and Go changes.
Tessa: I'll review redaction tests and the Python sample.
Leah: Thanks all 44d. I'll aim to have PR by EOD.
